Subject: Request: on-prem VPC attachment & egress mapping for StratusAI pilot

Hi Mina / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the quick sync last week. We're moving forward with a small on-prem pilot (2 racks) and need a short architecture review focused on how Redwood's control plane attaches to our VPC, the expected egress paths, and options to guarantee EU-only data residency for keys/logs/telemetry. High level:

- Control plane will be hosted in a Stratus-managed VPC in Frankfurt.
- Data plane (inference workers) will live on-prem in our DC; the control plane needs to reach management APIs and metrics ingestion endpoints.
- We cannot allow any customer data to egress to non-EU regions; audit logs and model KV caches can be handled locally if needed.

Could you review the attached network diagram and call out:
- Required inbound/outbound ports between control plane and agents (TCP/UDP + ports)
- Recommended TLS mutual-auth pattern for agent registration (we're using Vault PKI)
- Egress restrictions and validation checks to ensure EU-only telemetry endpoints
- Any suggested firewall/NAT placement and failover modes

We're targeting a pilot-ready design by the end of the month and would like a 30m review next week. Attachments: stratus-network-diagram-v1.pdf, fw-rules-export-jan2026.csv

Cheers,
Alex Jordan
Head of Infrastructure Operations
StratusAI

Hi Alex — thanks, received the diagram. Happy to take this on. Quick confirmations before the review:

- Are the two on-prem racks in the same L2/L3 boundary (single datacenter) or split across two zones in Frankfurt? That affects our KV cache failover pattern.
- Confirm Vault PKI will issue short-lived certs for agent bootstrap (yes/no). If not, we'll propose a bootstrap CA + mTLS with periodic rotation.

I've attached a first-pass Redwood reference draw.io that maps our usual control-plane endpoints and a suggested NAT/failover layout for egress restriction. Key points I'll cover in the review:
- Control plane <-> agent: mTLS on TCP 443 with keepalive, agent-initiated to avoid opening inbound ports to DC.
- Metrics/telemetry: configurable endpoints; can be pointed to EU-only collectors. We recommend shunting logs to a customer-managed S3/GCS in region and sending only anonymized heartbeat metrics to Redwood.
- KV/cache: recommend local LRU cache with periodic encrypted snapshot replication to customer bucket (no PII).

Proposed times for a 30m review: Wed 14 Jan 09:00-11:00 CET or Thu 15 Jan 08:00-12:00 CET. Let me know what works and we'll include a short Ops/Network checklist.

Attachments: redwood-vpc-reference.drawio

Best,

Folks — adding a few notes from an infra/runtime perspective. Quoting Mina's plan below for context.

On Tue, 13 Jan 2026 at 18:22 Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> I've attached a first-pass Redwood reference draw.io that maps our usual control-plane endpoints and a suggested NAT/failover layout for egress restriction. Key points I'll cover in the review:
> - Control plane <-> agent: mTLS on TCP 443 with keepalive, agent-initiated to avoid opening inbound ports to DC.
> - Metrics/telemetry: configurable endpoints; can be pointed to EU-only collectors. We recommend shunting logs to a customer-managed S3/GCS in region and sending only anonymized heartbeat metrics to Redwood.
> - KV/cache: recommend local LRU cache with periodic encrypted snapshot replication to customer bucket (no PII).

Technical notes / adjustments:
- Control plane traffic patterns: short-lived REST for control messages + long-lived websocket for control-commands and streaming logs. Recommend ALB/NLB in front of control plane endpoints depending on protocol.
- Agent registration: prefer client cert (Vault PKI) + registration token tied to HW ID. That combination reduces risk of token theft.
- Egress enforcement: use forced routing via customer egress appliance (explicit proxy) with a deny-by-default policy. For failover (if egress appliance loses uplink), agents should buffer and only send metadata/heartbeat to a queued EU-only endpoint.
- Ports: 443 outbound for control, 5222 for peer heartbeats if you use XMPP-style federation (not required), 22 blocked except through bastion for sysadmin access.

I'll prep a short 'ops checklist' for the review: firewall rules, cert rotation cadence, NAT mapping steps, and a minimal packet capture test to validate egress.

- Marcus
